bindings.note: be-bru/regulations/housing/rent_and_relocation_allowances.yaml, rule brussels_housing_rent_allowance_housing_conditions_met requires 'not brussels_housing_dwelling_managed_by_public_social_housing_or_social_rental_agency and ... not brussels_housing_dwelling_has_socialized_public_housing_rent' (Brussels Government order of 15 July 2021, article 3 section 3). brussels_housing_relocation_housing_conditions_met (order of 13 October 2022, article 3 section 3) and brussels_housing_relocation_rent_support_extinction_condition_applies (article 7) test the same pair, and every one of the three formulas uses only the union of the two inputs. Tenure's two social-rent categories stand in for this input. The concept splits social renting by landlord type (public authority or non-profit), while the input names who manages the dwelling (public social housing or a social rental agency). Public-authority renting at a socialized rent belongs to the separate input brussels_housing_dwelling_has_socialized_public_housing_rent, which is left uncovered, but it is flagged here instead. Because the consuming formulas read only the union, results are the same as long as that input stays false. A public-authority dwelling that is neither managed by a social housing operator nor let at a socialized rent is also flagged true. The concept is the state at the survey reference date; the rules are evaluated per month (period Month).

be-bru/regulations/housing/rent_and_relocation_allowances.yaml: brussels_housing_rent_allowance_monthly_amount = 'min(brussels_housing_monthly_rent_at_lease_start, brussels_housing_rent_allowance_uncapped_indexed_monthly_amount)' when eligible (Brussels Government order of 15 July 2021, articles 2, 3, 4 and 29). brussels_housing_relocation_monthly_rent_intervention_amount caps its amount with the same input (order of 13 October 2022, articles 2, 4, 7 and 19). Transform: monthly = annual / 12. The input is the monthly rent fixed when the lease began. The concept is the contract rent charged over the reference year, which includes any change since the lease began, so for older leases the two can differ. The concept excludes separately billed utilities and service charges, and the module does not say whether the lease-start rent includes charges. The concept is zero for owners and rent-free occupiers, for whom the allowances' lease conditions fail anyway.

be-bru/regulations/housing/rent_and_relocation_allowances.yaml, rule brussels_housing_rent_allowance_housing_conditions_met begins 'brussels_housing_principal_residence_lease and brussels_housing_rented_dwelling_in_brussels and ...' (Brussels Government order of 15 July 2021, article 3 section 3). brussels_housing_relocation_housing_conditions_met requires '(brussels_housing_principal_residence_lease or brussels_housing_transit_housing_occupancy_agreement)' (order of 13 October 2022, article 3 section 3). Renting tenure, in any of the three rented categories, stands in for holding a principal-residence lease. The input is a legal lease category that the module does not define, while tenure says only that the household rents the dwelling it lives in, not under which lease regime. A renter under another arrangement is flagged true here, for example a transit-housing occupancy agreement, which the relocation rule lists separately. Owners and rent-free occupiers are false.

be-bru/statutes/disability/elderly_care_allowance.yaml, rule brussels_apa_age_condition_met (COCOM ordinance of 10 December 2020 on APA, article 4 item 1 as amended by ordinance of 12 February 2026, articles 7 to 9; version effective 2026-02-20): 'brussels_apa_age_years >= belgium_disability_elderly_care_allowance_min_age_years'. That threshold is imported from be/statutes/disability/allowances.yaml as 65 (federal law of 27 February 1987, article 2 section 3), with excerpt 'accordée à la personne handicapée âgée d'au moins 65 ans'. Difference: the module does not say at which date (application or decision) age is read. The concept is completed years at the survey reference date.

be-bru/statutes/disability/elderly_care_allowance.yaml, rule brussels_apa_household_exists (COCOM order of 28 January 2021, article 4): 'if brussels_apa_cohabits_with_person_who_is_not_close_relative and not brussels_apa_household_member_detained_or_in_social_defense: 1'. brussels_apa_household_exists has two effects. It makes brussels_apa_income_disregard_category_code select the article 24 category B disregard rather than category A (17,762.27 rather than 14,214.53 EUR before indexation). When both members are entitled, it also triggers the article 5 section 2 half-income split (excerpt 'la personne avec laquelle il forme un ménage'). The module does not excerpt article 4's definition of which relatives are excluded. Differences: (1) the concept flags only a co-resident spouse, civil partner or cohabiting partner, so the input is broader than the concept. A claimant sharing the dwelling with a non-partner who is not a close relative, such as a friend or lodger, is missed. (2) The concept does not itself test the relative-degree exclusion. (3) The concept is the state at the survey reference date; the rule is annual.

be-bru/statutes/disability/elderly_care_allowance.yaml, rule brussels_apa_built_property_cadastral_income_exemption_amount (COCOM order of 28 January 2021, article 9): 'brussels_apa_built_property_cadastral_income_exemption + brussels_apa_built_property_cadastral_income_exemption_per_dependent_child * brussels_apa_dependent_child_count'. The excerpt reads 'Ce montant est majoré de 250,00 EUR pour chaque enfant à charge.' brussels_apa_built_property_deemed_annual_income subtracts the exemption from built-property cadastral income under max(0, ...), so the count has no effect while brussels_apa_built_property_cadastral_income is zero. Differences: (1) co-resident persons of any age who name the claimant as a parent stand in for children 'à charge', which the module does not define. Dependent children living elsewhere are missed, and co-resident adult children who are not dependent are counted. APA claimants are 65 or older (brussels_apa_age_condition_met), so their co-resident children are usually adults, and this over-count is the main error. (2) Children of a co-resident partner who do not name the claimant as a parent are not counted.

be-bru/statutes/disability/elderly_care_allowance.yaml, rule brussels_apa_property_deemed_annual_income (COCOM order of 28 January 2021, article 15): 'max(0, brussels_apa_property_deemed_annual_income_before_mortgage_interest - brussels_apa_eligible_annual_mortgage_interest)'. The interest is deducted from the deemed income of built and unbuilt property. The article 9 excerpt counts 'biens immobiliers bâtis que le bénéficiaire ou la personne avec laquelle il forme un ménage possède'. brussels_apa_annual_income_before_disregard then multiplies the summed income by brussels_apa_household_income_split_factor, so each claimant's input is the amount for the claimant together with the person with whom the claimant forms a household. Article 15's eligibility conditions are not excerpted in the module. Both values are annual. Differences: (1) the concept is interest on loans secured on the household's own dwelling only, while the rule may also cover loans on other property. (2) The household amount is placed on the household reference person, following the policyengine-us binding of home_mortgage_interest. A claimant who is the reference person's partner receives zero, although the shared mortgage counts for both partners in the rule. A claimant living in an adult child's home also receives zero. That matches the rule when the loan is the child's, because the APA household requires cohabitation with a person who is not a close relative. (3) Until brussels_apa_built_property_cadastral_income and brussels_apa_unbuilt_property_cadastral_income are bound, the deduction floors at zero and has no effect.

be-bru/statutes/property_tax/be_home_premium.yaml, rule brussels_be_home_household_conditions_met = 'brussels_be_home_household_has_member_with_real_right and brussels_be_home_household_domiciled_in_dwelling and brussels_be_home_situation_is_january_1' (Brussels ordinance of 23 November 2017, article 14, paragraphs 1 and 4). The module summary describes the premium as for 'a dwelling where the household is domiciled and at least one household member holds a real right'. The binding reads the Property row as the household's own dwelling. That is the only row where the premium can be nonzero, because the household must be domiciled there. The module itself does not assume this: brussels_be_home_household_domiciled_in_dwelling is a separate input. So the binding holds only when the adapter builds the Property row as the household's own dwelling. Owner tenure (owned_outright or owned_with_mortgage) stands in for 'a household member holds a real right'. The ordinance's real right is a legal category that the module does not define, and tenure records only ownership of the occupied dwelling. The concept is the state at the survey reference date; the rule uses the 1 January situation.

be-bru/statutes/property_tax/be_home_premium.yaml (Brussels ordinance of 23 November 2017, article 14). brussels_be_home_property_tax_deduction = 'min(max(0, brussels_be_home_property_tax_before_premium), brussels_be_home_premium_amount)' and brussels_be_home_property_tax_after_premium = 'max(0, brussels_be_home_property_tax_before_premium - brussels_be_home_property_tax_deduction)'. The module summary calls this 'a property-tax notice deduction interface' for the BE HOME premium, which is paid for 'a dwelling where the household is domiciled and at least one household member holds a real right'. The concept's own definition names the Belgian withholding tax on immovable property as the owner-liable recurrent tax on the dwelling. Group rule: Property is not a person unit, so this binding holds only if the adapter builds the household's own dwelling as a Property row and treats it as the unit containing the reference person. That is the same premise as this mapping's household_value binding brussels_be_home_household_has_member_with_real_right. household_value is rejected for amounts, and allocate_to_reference_unit also keeps the amount off any other Property row the household may have. Differences: (1) The concept is before all rebates or reductions, and the module does not say which reductions the notice amount already reflects, so the concept can exceed the input. (2) The concept is the household's own liability, so it is 0 for renters, whereas the notice on a rented dwelling carries the landlord's tax. The premium is unaffected because renters fail the real-right gate, but brussels_be_home_property_tax_after_premium reads 0 on such rows. (3) The premium uses the 1 January situation (brussels_be_home_situation_is_january_1); the concept is the reference year's liability.

Consumed in be-dg/statutes/family_benefits/eligibility.yaml by german_speaking_community_family_benefits_article_9_10_age_or_status_condition_met (Month). It is also consumed by german_speaking_community_family_benefits_article_12_13_missing_or_abducted_condition_met, and it reaches be/statutes/family_benefits/regional_routing.yaml through that module's import of be-dg eligibility. Consumed in be-dg/statutes/family_benefits/eligibility.yaml by german_speaking_community_family_benefits_article_9_10_age_or_status_condition_met (Month; decree of 23 April 2018 articles 9, 10, 11 and 14). With the german_speaking_community_family_benefits_ prefix dropped from every name, the branch reads 'child_age_years < final_age_cap_years and child_in_training and not employment_suspends_training_or_extension_entitlement'. It is reached only when the child is 18 or older and the disability branch fails. The module summary says 'Delegated residence, training, employment, and impairment proof rules remain supplied inputs'. The decree (article 9 section 3) leaves what counts as training to the Government, and the module does not encode that definition. The binding reads training as current enrollment in any ISCED programme at the reference date, not in the benefit month. The concept does not observe whatever programme-type or minimum-intensity conditions the delegated rules impose, and part-time enrollment counts as enrolled here. The employment-suspension input stays uncovered.

Consumed in be-vlg/statutes/education/school_allowance.yaml by flanders_school_allowance_amount (Year; Groeipakket decree arts 46-48). The formula first tests 'flanders_school_allowance_education_level == flanders_school_level_code_preschool' (code 1) and then pays flanders_school_allowance_indexed_preschool_amount. Otherwise it pays 0 when flanders_school_allowance_type equals flanders_school_type_code_none. Otherwise it tests 'flanders_school_allowance_education_level == flanders_school_level_code_primary' (code 2) for the primary amounts, and every other code gets the secondary amounts. flanders_school_level_code_secondary is 3. The module summary limits the allowance to pupils in preschool (kleuteronderwijs), primary (lager onderwijs) and secondary (secundair onderwijs) education. ISCED enrollment maps early_childhood to 1, primary to 2 and lower/upper secondary to 3. The rule has no code for a non-pupil, so not_enrolled, post_secondary_non_tertiary and tertiary get 0. Code 0 falls through to the secondary branch, so a non-pupil row is paid the secondary amount unless its allowance type is none. These rows need a pupil/eligibility gate that this module does not encode. The concept's early_childhood band also covers ISCED 01 provision for children under 3, which is not kleuteronderwijs, and the preschool branch pays with no income test. Period: the concept is point-in-time enrollment at the reference date, while the rule is annual.
